Ensure omnichannel initiatives are designed and driven by identified and relevant cross-country needs, delivering seamless integration between scientific engagement and marketing campaigns. d36c50bbb364ef0d.description: About the Role Ma’aden is seeking a Principal Specialist, Data Modeling & Arch Enterprise . Design data product models and curated layer schemas that support enterprise reporting, analytics, AI use cases, and downstream integrations. Ensure models address performance, maintainability, scalability, auditability, lineage, and future reuse across platforms and domains. Establish enterprise modeling standards, naming conventions, guidelines, reusable templates, and quality expectations for delivery teams. Partner with data governance teams to align business glossary definitions, stewardship ownership, metadata, lineage, and critical data elements. Review and approve modeling deliverables from internal teams and external vendors to ensure architectural consistency and quality. Lead the creation and optimization of data product schemas, curated layers, semantic structures, and consumption-ready models. Define modeling approaches for relational, non-relational, time-series, streaming, lakehouse, warehouse, and analytical platform requirements. Ensure data models support time-variant structures, historical traceability, auditability, semantic consistency, and trusted analytics consumption. Coordinate with data engineering, platform, analytics, AI, and enterprise architecture teams to ensure models are technically feasible and reusable. Define integration patterns that ensure consistent transformation logic, metadata, lineage, and data quality across source-to-consumption pipelines. Align operational, corporate, and analytical data structures to enable reliable reporting, analytics, AI enablement, and downstream system integration. Identify and resolve modeling inconsistencies, duplication, semantic gaps, and integration challenges across domains and platforms. Ensure data is modeled for trusted consumption by business users, data engineers, analysts, data scientists, and application teams. Mentor data modelers, data engineers, analysts, and delivery teams on modeling standards, patterns, review practices, and quality expectations. Lead model reviews, resolve design trade-offs, and guide teams on semantic consistency, reusability, performance, and maintainability. Document architecture decisions, model assumptions, standards exceptions, and reusable design guidance for enterprise adoption. Outcomes of Success Successful performance in this role will be demonstrated by enterprise conceptual, logical, and physical data models that are standardized, scalable, reusable, and aligned with business domains. Curated layers and data product schemas will support trusted reporting, analytics, AI enablement, and downstream consumption. Metadata, lineage, data quality, stewardship, and governance expectations will be embedded into modeling and integration patterns. Delivery teams will receive strong modeling assurance, coaching, and practical design guidance, leading to reduced duplication and improved reuse.

d341246320a22546.description: About the Role HCLTech is seeking a PMO Senior Manager for Technology Governance & Delivery, specializing in QA & Co-ordination, to join their team in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. This full-time role requires 3-5 years of experience and focuses on leading independent quality assurance and site co-ordination for City Ops ICT assets throughout the project lifecycle. The manager will establish and operate consistent quality controls, stage-gate checkpoints, inspection and testing arrangements, and evidence-based validation of operational requirements before handover and service transition. The position involves maintaining objective oversight of gaps, defects, and remediation, while ensuring delivery accountability remains with the relevant project, contractor, vendor, or asset owner. Key Responsibilities QA Governance & Independence: Own and maintain the City Ops ICT QA/QC and gap-assessment framework, including standards, workflows, evidence requirements, severity classification, validation, prioritization, closure, and reporting. Define QA checkpoints, sign-off criteria, Site Inspection Plans, asset-specific checklists, test scripts, hold/witness points, and acceptance evidence standards. Provide independent assessment of operational readiness and quality, challenging incomplete evidence and escalating material acceptance risks. Lead the QA team, applying consistent methods across sites and packages. Site Co-ordination, Inspection & Testing: Plan and co-ordinate site access, inspections, permits, inductions, vendor attendance, equipment, and documentation for site verification activities. Direct and quality-assure document reviews, physical inspections, interviews, and functional testing. Co-ordinate physical and functional verification of ICT infrastructure and systems, ensuring inspection records contain necessary evidence and clear outcomes. Operational Readiness & Handover Assurance: Translate approved service, support, monitoring, resilience, cybersecurity, lifecycle, and non-functional requirements into measurable acceptance criteria. Validate readiness evidence, test and commissioning results, as-built and configuration records, asset information, licenses, warranties, training, O&M documentation, and support arrangements. Provide evidence-based recommendations on handover readiness, documenting exceptions, residual risks, and corrective actions. Confirm outstanding defects and vendor obligations are transferred into appropriate operational governance processes. Issue Management, Reporting & Escalation: Own and maintain the Master Gap Register, Defect/Snag Register, and Remediation Tracker as controlled records. Validate findings for evidence sufficiency, severity, ownership, and corrective action, tracking target dates and verifying objective closure evidence. Escalate critical findings, disputed classifications, safety concerns, and unresolved readiness risks through agreed governance channels. Prepare dashboards, executive summaries, and decision-ready reports on quality status, leading root-cause reviews and continuous improvement. Stakeholder & Team Co-ordination: Co-ordinate inspections, validation workshops, and readiness reviews with internal and external stakeholders including City Ops ICT, QTech, MDU/EBU, Districts, Cybersecurity, vendors, contractors, and service integrators. Provide work direction and coaching to field/test engineers and support consistent technical and audit-ready quality records. Seven Stage-Gate Quality Checkpoints CP1 – Understand Project Scope: Confirm asset/system scope, site constraints, applicable standards, stakeholders, and QA approach. CP2 – Define City ICT Operations Requirements: Translate operational, service, and non-functional requirements into measurable acceptance criteria. CP3 – Review Procurement Packages: Review RFPs, BoQs, and specifications for inspection, testing, handover, support, and evidence provisions. CP4 – Review Material Submissions: Review technical/material submissions, methods, and test plans; flag deviations and lifecycle impacts. CP5 – Verify Delivered Requirements: Witness inspections and tests, validate as-built/configuration evidence, and track defects to closure. CP6 – Support Handover Acceptance: Review handover packs and readiness evidence; recommend acceptance, exceptions, and corrective actions. CP7 – Service Management Transition: Confirm quality records, support procedures, and open obligations are transferred into operational governance. Qualifications and Experience 3-5 years of relevant experience. Demonstrated ability to lead independent quality assurance functions. Experience with establishing and operating consistent quality controls and stage-gate checkpoints. Proficiency in managing defect remediation and maintaining objective oversight of project delivery. Internal and External Engagement The role involves significant interaction with various internal and external stakeholders. Internally, this includes the Technology Governance & Delivery Lead, PMO, City Systems, City ICT Infrastructure, Operational Readiness, Cybersecurity, and operational asset owners. Externally, engagement will be with QTech, MDU/EBU, Districts, delivery teams, system integrators, contractors, vendors, and specialist field/test engineers.

d326c703d293aabb.job_title: Chief Clinical Officer (CCO) (Senior Healthcare Experience Essential) 50013023
d326c703d293aabb.description: JOB PURPOSE Key internal interfaces include the CEO, executive leadership team, healthcare asset leaders, quality and patient safety teams, clinical operations, digital health, legal and compliance, talent acquisition, and partnership teams. Key external interfaces include regulators, accreditation bodies, clinical partners, academic institutions, sports federations, professional teams, and other strategic healthcare partners. The Chief Medical Officer (CMO) is QHC’s most senior clinical executive and the single accountable owner of enterprise clinical strategy, medical governance, quality, patient and athlete safety, and clinical standards across all QHC healthcare assets. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the CMO brings clinical leadership, standards-setting, assurance, and medical advisory authority under one role, ensuring clear and consistent clinical accountability while operational delivery remains with the respective healthcare businesses and functions. The CMO ensures that clinical delivery across all QHC healthcare assets follows the QHC’s clinical and wellness standards, quality expectations, and readiness requirements, reflecting international evidence-based practice and applicable Saudi regulatory requirements. As a member of the QHC executive leadership team, the CMO translates the Kingdom's Vision 2030 and Qiddiya’s healthcare ambitions into governed, accountable practice, championing patient and athlete safety, clinical research and academic collaboration, and positioning QHC as a regionally recognized centre of clinical excellence. KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES The role sets enterprise clinical standards, quality expectations, and governance requirements for all QHC healthcare assets, while day-to-day operational delivery, staffing deployment, and business-unit execution remain accountable to the relevant operating leaders. 1. Enterprise Clinical Strategy & Medical Affairs • Provide overall clinical leadership and set the enterprise clinical strategy for QHC across all current and future service lines, in alignment with the QIC and Vision 2030 healthcare transformation objectives. • Serve as the principal clinical voice on the executive leadership team, advising the CEO / MD and the Board and Medical Advisory Committee on clinical strategy, service development, clinical risk and medical policy. • Provide clinical and wellness input into service models and define the clinical standards, quality expectations and readiness requirements for all healthcare assets. • Represent QHC's clinical capabilities to sports federations, professional teams, government stakeholders, regulators and strategic partners. 2. Clinical Governance, Quality & Patient / Athlete Safety • Establish QHC’s overarching clinical governance and quality framework, setting expectations for patient and athlete safety, clinical quality, risk and compliance across all healthcare assets. • Provide a consistent enterprise-wide framework for clinical quality and accountability, ensuring clear standards and expectations across all healthcare assets. • Define, monitor, and report enterprise clinical KPIs and quality dashboards for clinical partnership or assets under direct operation of QHC. • Define clinical governance and escalation requirements, ensure appropriate review of priority quality, safety, and service issues, and provide senior clinical guidance on corrective actions, risk mitigation, and follow-up accountability. 3. Clinical Excellence, Protocols & Care Pathways • Set QHC’s enterprise clinical excellence, safety and wellness standards across all healthcare assets, aligned with evidence-based international practice and applicable Saudi regulatory requirements • Provide clinical and wellness guidance to all healthcare assets on service models, safety requirements and areas for clinical improvement • Develop and continuously review clinical policies, evidence-based care pathways, treatment protocols and standard operating procedures of clinical partners and QHC operated assets aligned with international best practice. • Promote evidence-based, person-centred models of care that integrate physical, psychological and social dimensions of health, wellbeing and performance, as relevant to the populations served. • Set enterprise clinical requirements for documentation, information governance, patient confidentiality and related clinical compliance, in line with applicable Saudi regulatory requirements and relevant international standards. 4. Sports Medicine & Citywide Healthcare Clinical Advisory • Provide clinical and wellness advisory support to all healthcare assets, providing input into service models, clinical readiness requirements, quality expectations and relevant performance measures. • Advise on multidisciplinary and integrated approaches to care, supporting alignment with QHC’s clinical standards and evidence-based practice. • Provide clinical guidance on priority service areas and readiness requirements, identifying clinical gaps, risks and opportunities for improvement. 5. Partnerships, Research & Academic Collaboration • Contribute to the development and implementation of clinical partnerships with institutions by supporting knowledge exchange, capability building, and the integration of leading practices into clinical care. • Support research, innovation, and academic collaboration initiatives, facilitating clinical engagement in research, education, and evidence-generation activities. • Participate in evaluating and adopting emerging clinical technologies, digital health solutions, and clinical analytics that enhance clinical practice and support data-driven decision-making. Role success will be measured by the design and deployment of all QHC healthcare assets, engagement of QHC clinical partnerships, achievement of clinical readiness milestones, compliance with applicable Saudi regulatory and accreditation requirements, adoption of approved clinical standards and care pathways, strength of clinical partner engagement, and sustained improvement in patient and athlete safety, quality and cost indicators through value based care. EXPERIENCE & ACADEMIC QUALIFICATIONS Medical degree (MD, MBBS, MBChB, or equivalent) with board certification or postgraduate specialty qualification in a relevant discipline is required. Additional qualifications or experience in clinical leadership, sports medicine, population health or related fields are preferred Active registration and licensure with the Saudi Commission for Health Specialties (SCFHS) at Consultant level, or clear eligibility for SCFHS Consultant classification, is required. Dataflow primary source verification and SCFHS Mumaris Plus registration must be completed prior to commencement. 15+ years of progressive clinical experience, with a substantial track record in senior clinical leadership, medical director or chief-level roles within accredited healthcare institutions. Experience delivering care to professional athletes, elite teams or comparable high-performance environments is highly desirable. Proven expertise in clinical governance, patient-safety management, multidisciplinary team leadership and quality improvement within a regulated healthcare environment. Prior experience in JCI and/or CBAHI accredited institutions and within partnership or joint-venture clinical models is highly preferred. Strong working knowledge of Saudi MOH and SCFHS licensing and regulatory frameworks, and of the clinical operating requirements of a startup or greenfield healthcare organization.
